input.rationale: Section 13.5 allocates ownership of Developments (interface coding and programs created solely by Corio to run the Software on the Corio Servers) to Corio, but the "unless" carve-out flips ownership of our own work product to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to us. That is an assignment of our IP to the vendor and contradicts our preferred position that we own deliverables and work product created for us. The redline deletes the ownership flip and instead gives Commerce One a nonexclusive, royalty-free support licence (preserving the commercial rationale for the carve-out), and adds a confirmation that Corio and its Customers' data hosted on the Corio Servers is not assigned to Commerce One, which the agreement otherwise omits. Commerce One's retained ownership of the Software itself (Section 2.8) and of its pre-existing materials is unchanged and acceptable.

proposal.summary: Corio retains ownership of Developments it creates (support licence instead of ownership transfer) and confirms ownership of Corio/Customer data
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13.5 currently transfers ownership of Developments we create to Commerce One whenever it supports them on an ongoing basis; our position is that we own what we pay for and create, so we have replaced that transfer with a support licence back to Commerce One. We have also confirmed that no data of Corio or its Customers is assigned to Commerce One.
